reflexion_entries_to_archive.text: S138 P1: my Council prompt stated that structuralSignature is SIZE-ONLY (true) but never mentioned that the differential rig actually compares hashWorldStateFull. Both Grok and Gemini then reasoned correctly from that incomplete set and CONVERGED on the same wrong conclusion - abandon per-primitive hp, the rig will be blind to non-lethal damage. Gemini even prescribed a remedy (add an XOR checksum of primitive hps to the worker signature) that was pure unnecessary work. The failure mode is the dangerous one: a partial fact set does not make a Council say 'uncertain', it makes them AGREE, and agreement reads as confirmation. Two independent seats converging is only evidence if the premises were complete. Fix: when briefing external reviewers, state not just what a mechanism IS but which consumers actually call it - and treat unanimous agreement with my own framing as the weakest possible signal, not the strongest.

S138 P1: the whole design rested on a claim in a docblock - that stateHashFull has a FIELD-LEVEL guard which fails tsc by name if you add a field to an already-hashed entity. That is a claim ABOUT a compile-time behaviour, which is exactly the class PRIME-AUDIT's runtime-verifiability question exists for. So step 1 of execution was to add hp?: number to Primitive, touch nothing else, and run tsc. It failed with ERROR_UNCOVERED_FIELD: "hp" at stateHashFull.ts:246. Two minutes, and it converted a cited assumption into a fact - and simultaneously refuted a reviewer who had asserted the opposite. When a docblock makes a falsifiable claim you are about to depend on, run it.

S138 P2: the owner reported 'each primitive pushes another primitive away as anti-magnetism'. The obvious suspect was the collision solver, and I could have spent the session tuning resolveCollisions. anchorStabilize.ts:9-11 refuted it outright in prose someone had already written down: placed primitives are NOT free-integrated, verletStepAll steps only freeSparks, resolveCollisions is spark-only, a structure is held purely by solveBonds constraints. The real culprit was STRUCTURE_GROW_IMPULSE - a cosmetic 'puff' from S13 that was in fact an unconditional outward physics impulse written into settled geometry on EVERY placement. Lesson: before chasing the plausible subsystem, grep for whether someone already documented that it CANNOT be the cause. The codebase often knows.

S138 P2: moving the keep ring 275 -> 420 broke 4 e2e tests that had nothing to do with keeps. Cause: castle-panel.spec.ts:24 contained 'CANVAS_WIDTH / 2 - (125 + 150)' - a hand-copy of SPAWNER_RADIUS + 150 - under a comment explaining the derivation. The comment made it look careful; it was the bug. e2e/helpers.ts had ALREADY learned this exact lesson in S137 and installed __SPARK__.keepCenter with a note that 'the harness now cannot disagree with the game about where a castle is' - but only one file adopted it. Fix was to export keepAnchor and ask the app, never to update the copy. When you delete a duplicated constant, grep for every OTHER transcription of the same formula in the same commit.

S138 P1: I made Primitive.hp REQUIRED rather than hp?: number, arguing that an optional field forces 'hp ?? MAX' at every read and the forgotten one is the bug. The choice paid for itself within one tsc run: 57 errors, of which three were PRODUCTION sites (botSpawnerSeed.ts:92,159,180) that construct Primitive literals directly and would have minted shapes with hp: undefined - turning every later 'prim.hp -= amount' into NaN, a silent un-killable primitive that no test would have caught. The other 54 were test fixtures, i.e. cheap. Paying a mechanical fixture cost to convert a whole class of silent runtime bug into a compile error is almost always the right trade.

S138 close: MCV hard-failed on two file_lacks assertions - lacks('SPAWNER_RADIUS + 150') and lacks('CANVAS_WIDTH / 2 - (125 + 150)') - because the very commits that REMOVED those expressions from the code added comments QUOTING them to explain what changed and why. S137 recorded this exact trap ('file_lacks needles match COMMENTS too') and I walked into it again, because good commenting practice actively creates the collision: the better you document a removal, the more likely the needle survives. Durable fix: never assert file_lacks on a bare expression. Assert the CODE form that prose cannot plausibly reproduce - 'const r = SPAWNER_RADIUS + 150', 'const KEEP0' - or assert file_contains on the replacement instead.

S138 P1: my real-physics acceptance test imported PHYSICS_DT from constants.ts, where it does not exist (it lives in physicsLoop.ts). vitest does not typecheck, so SUBSTEP_DT was NaN and the test PASSED - because solveBonds is purely positional and the fixture had no free sparks for verletStepAll to ruin. So the assertions were valid but the test was not exercising what its name claimed. Only tsc caught it. Two habits from this: run tsc before believing a new test, and add a cheap guard (expect(Number.isFinite(SUBSTEP_DT))) so a degenerate input can never masquerade as a pass again.

S138 P2: removing STRUCTURE_GROW_IMPULSE broke 5 tests in session13.test.ts that existed specifically to assert the outward puff, with careful comments deriving the expected 0.8px offsets. Deleting them would have erased the record that the behaviour was ever deliberate, and left no guard against someone reintroducing it. I inverted them instead - same fixtures, now asserting prevPos === pos - with a header explaining that the owner reclassified the behaviour as a defect, plus one NEW test proving only the OUTWARD half went (the inward MERGE_IMPULSE still fires on a merge). A test that pinned a removed behaviour is not dead weight; inverted, it is the strongest guard you have against the removal being quietly undone.

Of ~8 challenges across two seats, 4 were technically specific and ALL 4 were empirically false; the one adopted finding (there is no shared raze path — two ad-hoc primitives.delete sites duplicating a 4-step contract) corrected my own draft and materially de-risked the change. So the honest scoring is 1 material hit, 4 refuted criticals, 3 carry-forwards. That is the tenth recorded firing of #empirical-refutes-plausible-criticals — the pattern is now stable enough that the default posture on any reviewer critical should be 'grep it first', not 'triage it'.

MY SCOPE ESTIMATE FOR ITEM 3 WAS TOO HIGH, THE SAME DIRECTION AS S137's ORDER-OF-MAGNITUDE MISS. I flagged 'bots use gatherers' as potentially V6-1.7-scale (BACKLOG estimates ~130 lines of botBrain + ~130 of botController). Actual production change: roughly 40 lines — one pure predicate (isOwnPorchSpark), one candidate filter, one BotGoal member, one dispatch case. It was cheap because PULL_FROM_BANK, the bank, and per-seat gatherers had ALREADY shipped, and because pickTargetSpark draws rng() exactly once so filtering was replay-free. Same lesson as S137: when the codebase already contains most of the machinery, cost is a COUNT, not a guess — and A.0 is what converts one into the other.

THE THREE OWNER ITEMS WERE NOT EQUALLY WELL-DIAGNOSED BY THE OWNER, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF A.0. Item 1 mapped cleanly to an already-ruled design item (R4). Item 3 was exactly right — bots really did have two income channels. Item 2's MECHANISM was wrong (it was never collision; placed primitives are not free-integrated at all) while the SYMPTOM was completely real. Taking the report seriously while re-deriving the cause is what found STRUCTURE_GROW_IMPULSE — a five-year-old cosmetic 'puff' that was in fact unconditional physics on settled geometry.
retrospective: BRIEF EXTERNAL REVIEWERS WITH CONSUMERS, NOT JUST MECHANISMS. Saying 'structuralSignature is size-only' was true and produced a confident, unanimous, wrong verdict because I omitted '...and the differential rig compares hashWorldStateFull instead'. Next Council prompt: for every mechanism cited, name who actually calls it.

WHEN CHANGING A CONSTANT, GREP FOR ITS TRANSCRIPTIONS IN THE SAME COMMIT. The keep-ring move broke 4 e2e tests via a hand-copied 'CANVAS_WIDTH / 2 - (125 + 150)'. helpers.ts had already learned this in S137 and installed the __SPARK__.keepCenter getter — but only one file adopted it. A constant change is a search-and-adopt task, not an edit.

NEVER WRITE A LITERAL EXAMPLE OF A PATTERN INSIDE THE FILE THAT SUPPRESSES THAT PATTERN. This session hit the same shape THREE times: two MCV file_lacks needles matched the comments explaining the removals, and .gitleaksignore tripped its own rule by quoting a worked example. Documenting a pattern reproduces it. Assert on the CODE form; describe suppressed patterns in prose.

THE STRONGEST TEST THIS SESSION IS THE ONE THAT PINS A REFUTATION. damage.test.ts asserts that a NON-LETHAL 10-hp divergence changes hashWorldStateFull while every collection size stays identical. That encodes the Council's claim, the evidence against it, and a guard against anyone dropping hp from the wide projection later. Refutations are worth pinning, not just reporting.
